skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Delegates repository exploration and implementation to Google Antigravity CLI while Codex controls approval, review, verification, and delivery.
skill.summary: Delegate bounded repository work to AGY with reviewable workflows and verification controls.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: Of 400 static findings, 396 are lexical false positives from schema punctuation, defensive validation, documentation, or bounded local tooling. Confirmed risks are the external AGY launch, caller-selected verifier execution, and two legacy shell-verification paths. Default provider dispatch also creates a documented high-impact repository disclosure risk unless operators use a narrow approved scope. Static review was capped at 400/889 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 489 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Default dispatch can expose the complete disposable worktree to the external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Require provider scope by default and require a separate explicit override for whole-worktree transmission.

remediation.issue: Legacy verification evaluates caller-supplied text with bash.
remediation.suggestion: Deprecate shell verification and require canonical argv verification for marketplace installations.

remediation.issue: Verifier argv mode can execute any caller-selected local program.
remediation.suggestion: Require interactive confirmation for each verifier executable and keep credentials unavailable unless separately approved.

remediation.issue: Marketplace tool metadata lists Claude hosts while the skill documentation says they are unsupported.
remediation.suggestion: Align supported tool metadata with the documented Codex-only runtime requirement.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly state that the full worktree may be provider-readable and potentially transmitted. They also document approval and scoped-staging mitigations.

content.value_statement: Large repository tasks can exceed one agent context or require parallel investigation. This skill delegates bounded work to AGY while Codex reviews changes and verifies results.
actual_capabilities: Routes exploration, bounded implementation, and project-scale work through separate AGY workflows.
Creates disposable Git worktrees and owner-private state for delegated jobs.
Previews provider transmission and supports content-bound provider scopes.
Manages approved starts, resumes, restarts, continuations, cancellation, and finalization.
Builds verification copies and binds check evidence to the current candidate.
Provides model selection, compatibility checks, benchmarks, diagnostics, and evidence reports.
limitations: The runtime requires Codex CLI, Bash, Python, Git, AGY, and provider network access.
Claude and Claude Code hosts are not supported, despite provider models that may contain Claude names.
Default dispatch may expose the entire disposable worktree to Google or Gemini unless scoped.
The worktree is not a security sandbox, and users must review diffs and choose verification commands.

use_cases.description: Delegate a bounded inventory, then review cited files and coverage limits before planning changes.

use_cases.title: Implement a focused change

use_cases.title: Coordinate project-scale work

prompt_templates.title: Repository overview
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AGY to map this repository. Identify major components, entry points, tests, and unknown areas. Do not modify files.

best_practices: Review the exact provider scope and remove secrets before every dispatch.
Inspect the candidate diff and select verification commands independently.
Use separate planning, implementation, and acceptance contexts for material changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat installation or a prior approval as authorization for a new provider transmission.
Do not execute commands reported by the worker without independent review.
Do not claim correctness, security, or completion from provider success alone.

faq.question: What does this skill delegate?
faq.answer: It delegates repository exploration, bounded implementation, and project workflows to Google Antigravity CLI.

faq.question: Does it support Claude or Claude Code hosts?
faq.answer: No. The packaged instructions require Codex CLI, even when a provider model name contains Claude.

faq.question: What repository data can reach the provider?
faq.answer: Default mode may expose the entire disposable worktree. Provider scope mode stages only approved entries.

faq.question: Does the worktree sandbox AGY?
faq.answer: No. It isolates Git changes but does not provide filesystem, network, process, PATH, or same-user isolation.

faq.question: Who accepts the final changes?
faq.answer: Codex or the human operator reviews the actual diff, runs selected checks, and chooses the final disposition.

faq.question: Can it run verification commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Canonical argv mode avoids shell parsing, while legacy shell verification requires explicit acknowledgements.
